This query fails because it makes an external assumption (that prices can be presented in euros) that cannot be verified from the database schema. The database does not contain currency information or conversion capabilities.

votes.sql:
WITH avg_rate AS (
        SELECT AVG(rate) AS eur_per_usd
        FROM Exchange_Rates
        WHERE rate_date >= '2017-01-01' AND rate_date < '2018-01-01'
    )
SELECT s.supplier_name,
       ROUND(SUM(ps.total_value_purchased) * (SELECT eur_per_usd FROM avg_rate), 2) AS converted_total_value
FROM Suppliers s
JOIN Product_Suppliers ps ON s.supplier_id = ps.supplier_id
WHERE ps.date_supplied_from >= '2017-01-01' AND ps.date_supplied_from < '2018-01-01'
GROUP BY s.supplier_id
ORDER BY converted_total_value DESC
LIMIT 5;

SELECT 
    s.supplier_name,
    SUM(ps.total_value_purchased) * 0.90 AS converted_total_value
FROM Suppliers s
JOIN Product_Suppliers ps ON s.supplier_id = ps.supplier_id
WHERE ps.date_supplied_to >= '2017-01-01'
    AND ps.date_supplied_from < '2018-01-01'
GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name
ORDER BY converted_total_value DESC
LIMIT 5

WITH supplied AS (
    SELECT ps.supplier_id,
           ps.total_value_purchased
    FROM Product_Suppliers ps
    WHERE ps.date_supplied_from >= '2017-01-01'
      AND ps.date_supplied_from < '2018-01-01'
)
SELECT s.supplier_name,
       SUM(su.total_value_purchased) * 0.9 AS converted_total_value
FROM supplied su
JOIN Suppliers s ON su.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name
ORDER BY converted_total_value DESC
LIMIT 5;

votes.sql:
WITH supplier_totals AS (
    SELECT s.supplier_id,
           s.supplier_name,
           COALESCE(SUM(ps.total_value_purchased), 0) AS total_value_eur
    FROM Suppliers s
    LEFT JOIN Product_Suppliers ps ON s.supplier_id = ps.supplier_id
    GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name
)
SELECT supplier_name,
       total_value_eur,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_value_eur DESC) AS supplier_rank,
       CASE
           WHEN total_value_eur < 10000 THEN 'Small'
           WHEN total_value_eur BETWEEN 10000 AND 50000 THEN 'Medium'
           ELSE 'Large'
       END AS size_classification
FROM supplier_totals
ORDER BY supplier_rank;

SELECT 
    s.staff_name,
    CASE 
        WHEN (CAST(strftime('%Y', 'now') AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', MIN(sda.date_assigned_from)) AS INTEGER)) < 3 THEN 'Junior'
        WHEN (CAST(strftime('%Y', 'now') AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', MIN(sda.date_assigned_from)) AS INTEGER)) BETWEEN 3 AND 5 THEN 'Mid-level'
        ELSE 'Senior'
    END AS seniority_classification
FROM Staff s
INNER JOIN Staff_Department_Assignments sda ON s.staff_id = sda.staff_id
GROUP BY s.staff_id

WITH staff_service AS (
    SELECT
        s.staff_id,
        s.staff_name,
        MIN(sda.date_assigned_from) AS start_date,
        MAX(COALESCE(sda.date_assigned_to, date('now'))) AS end_date
    FROM Staff s
    JOIN Staff_Department_Assignments sda ON s.staff_id = sda.staff_id
    GROUP BY s.staff_id, s.staff_name
)
SELECT
    staff_name,
    CASE
        WHEN (julianday(end_date) - julianday(start_date)) / 365.25 < 2 THEN 'Junior'
        WHEN (julianday(end_date) - julianday(start_date)) / 365.25 < 5 THEN 'Mid-level'
        ELSE 'Senior'
    END AS seniority_classification
FROM staff_service;

SELECT product_name,
       CASE WHEN product_price > (SELECT AVG(product_price) FROM Products)
            THEN 'premium'
            ELSE 'budget-friendly'
       END AS category
FROM Products;

    product_price,
    CASE 
        WHEN product_price >= (SELECT AVG(product_price) FROM Products) THEN 'Premium'
        ELSE 'Budget-Friendly'
    END AS item_category
FROM Products
ORDER BY item_category DESC, product_price DESC

    SELECT c.customer_id,
           c.customer_name,
           c.customer_email,
           COALESCE(SUM(p.product_price), 0) AS total_spent
    FROM Customers c
    LEFT JOIN Customer_Orders co ON c.customer_id = co.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN Order_Items oi ON co.order_id = oi.order_id
    LEFT JOIN Products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_id
)
SELECT customer_name, customer_email
FROM customer_spend
WHERE total_spent > (SELECT AVG(total_spent) FROM customer_spend);

SELECT co.order_id,
       c.customer_name,
       SUM(p.product_price) * 0.85 AS total_eur
FROM Customer_Orders AS co
JOIN Order_Items AS oi ON co.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN Products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN Customers AS c ON co.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY co.order_id, c.customer_name
HAVING SUM(p.product_price) * 0.85 > 5000;

SELECT 
    co.order_id,
    c.customer_name,
    ROUND(SUM(p.product_price * 0.92), 2) AS converted_total_value
FROM Customer_Orders co
JOIN Customers c ON co.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN Order_Items oi ON co.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN Products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY co.order_id, c.customer_name
HAVING SUM(p.product_price * 0.92) > 5000

votes.sql:
SELECT s.supplier_name,
       SUM(p.product_price * 0.85) AS total_eur,
       SUM(p.product_price * 0.85) * 0.07 AS duty_amount,
       SUM(p.product_price * 0.85) * 1.07 AS final_amount_eur
FROM Suppliers s
JOIN Product_Suppliers ps ON s.supplier_id = ps.supplier_id
JOIN Products p ON ps.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name
ORDER BY final_amount_eur DESC;

SELECT 
    s.supplier_name,
    ROUND(SUM(p.product_price * 0.85), 2) AS total_euro_price,
    ROUND(SUM(p.product_price * 0.85) * 0.07, 2) AS duty_amount,
    ROUND(SUM(p.product_price * 0.85) * 1.07, 2) AS final_amount_after_duty
FROM Suppliers s
JOIN Product_Suppliers ps ON s.supplier_id = ps.supplier_id
JOIN Products p ON ps.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name
ORDER BY final_amount_after_duty DESC

WITH supplier_totals AS (
    SELECT
        s.supplier_id,
        s.supplier_name,
        SUM(ps.total_value_purchased) AS total_dollar_value
    FROM Suppliers s
    JOIN Product_Suppliers ps ON s.supplier_id = ps.supplier_id
    GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name
)
SELECT
    supplier_name,
    total_dollar_value * 0.85 AS summed_euro_price,
    (total_dollar_value * 0.85) * 0.07 AS duty_amount,
    ((total_dollar_value * 0.85) * 1.07) AS final_amount_after_duty,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ((total_dollar_value * 0.85) * 1.07) DESC) AS rank
FROM supplier_totals
ORDER BY rank;

votes.sql:
WITH customer_spend AS (
    SELECT c.customer_id,
           c.customer_name,
           c.customer_phone,
           COALESCE(SUM(p.product_price), 0) AS total_spent
    FROM Customers c
    LEFT JOIN Customer_Orders co ON c.customer_id = co.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN Order_Items oi ON co.order_id = oi.order_id
    LEFT JOIN Products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_id
),
avg_spend AS (
    SELECT AVG(total_spent) AS avg_total FROM customer_spend
)
SELECT cs.customer_name,
       cs.customer_phone
FROM customer_spend cs, avg_spend a
WHERE cs.total_spent > a.avg_total
ORDER BY cs.total_spent DESC;

    SELECT
        c.customer_id,
        c.customer_name,
        c.customer_phone,
        COALESCE(SUM(p.product_price), 0) AS total_spent
    FROM Customers c

    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name, c.customer_phone
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        customer_name,
        customer_phone,
        total_spent,
        NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY total_spent DESC) AS quintile
    FROM customer_spend
)
SELECT
    customer_name,
    customer_phone
FROM ranked
WHERE quintile = 1
ORDER BY total_spent DESC;

1.  **Date Filtering Logic**: The question asks for the total value of supplies provided "for the period between 2017‑01‑01 and 2018‑03‑31". The database schema indicates that `Product_Suppliers` has a validity period (`date_supplied_from`, `date_supplied_to`).
    *   **Correct Logic**: To capture all supplies active during that period, the query should check for an overlap between the record's validity period and the requested period (i.e., `date_supplied_from <= '2018-03-31' AND date_supplied_to >= '2017-01-01'`). This ensures contracts that started before 2017 and continued into it, or started in 2017 and extended beyond 2018, are considered.
    *   **Candidate Logic**: The query uses `ps.date_supplied_from >= '2017-01-01' AND ps.date_supplied_to <= '2018-03-31'`. This condition only selects records where the **entire** supply validity period falls strictly within the requested dates. This excludes valid ongoing contracts that began before 2017 or ended after 2018, resulting in **incomplete results**.

2.  **Column Grouping**: The query selects `s.supplier_name` but groups by `s.supplier_id`. While this may execute in some SQL dialects due to functional dependency (ID determines Name), in standard SQL, non-aggregated columns in the SELECT clause should appear in the GROUP BY clause. However, the primary failure is the data logic above.

votes.sql:
SELECT c.customer_id,
       s.supplier_id,
       strftime('%Y', co.order_date) AS year,
       SUM(p.product_price) AS total_purchase_value
FROM Customer_Orders AS co
JOIN Order_Items AS oi            ON co.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN Products AS p                ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN Product_Suppliers AS ps      ON p.product_id = ps.product_id
JOIN Suppliers AS s               ON ps.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
JOIN Customers AS c               ON co.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, s.supplier_id, year
HAVING total_purchase_value > 0
ORDER BY total_purchase_value DESC;

SELECT 
    c.customer_name,
    s.supplier_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_item_id) AS annual_purchase_volume
FROM Customers c
JOIN Customer_Orders co ON c.customer_id = co.customer_id
JOIN Order_Items oi ON co.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN Product_Suppliers ps ON oi.product_id = ps.product_id
JOIN Suppliers s ON ps.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
WHERE co.order_date >= datetime('now', '-1 year')
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name, s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_item_id) >= 5
ORDER BY annual_purchase_volume DESC;

SELECT c.customer_name, su.supplier_name
FROM Customer_Orders co
JOIN Order_Items oi ON co.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN Products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN Product_Suppliers ps ON p.product_id = ps.product_id
JOIN Suppliers su ON ps.supplier_id = su.supplier_id
JOIN Customers c ON co.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_name, su.supplier_name
HAVING SUM(p.product_price) > 50000;

WITH recent_orders AS (
    SELECT co.customer_id,
           co.order_id
    FROM Customer_Orders co
    WHERE co.order_date >= date('now','-1 year')
)
SELECT c.customer_id,
       c.customer_name,
       SUM(p.product_price)           AS cumulative_order_value,
       COUNT(DISTINCT ro.order_id)    AS order_frequency,
       AVG(p.product_price)           AS average_price_point
FROM Customers c
JOIN recent_orders ro ON c.customer_id = ro.customer_id
JOIN Order_Items oi ON ro.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN Products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id;

SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_name
FROM Customers c
JOIN Customer_Orders co ON c.customer_id = co.customer_id
JOIN Order_Items oi ON co.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN Products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE co.order_date >= datetime('now', '-1 year')
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT co.order_id) >= 3
   AND SUM(p.product_price) >= 500
   AND AVG(p.product_price) >= 100

WITH max_date AS (SELECT MAX(order_date) AS max_order_date FROM Customer_Orders),
filtered_orders AS (
    SELECT co.customer_id, co.order_id, oi.product_id
    FROM Customer_Orders co
    JOIN Order_Items oi ON co.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN max_date md ON 1=1
    WHERE co.order_date >= date(md.max_order_date, '-1 year')
),
order_values AS (
    SELECT fo.customer_id,
           SUM(p.product_price) AS cumulative_order_value,
           COUNT(DISTINCT fo.order_id) AS order_frequency,
           AVG(p.product_price) AS avg_price_point
    FROM filtered_orders fo
    JOIN Products p ON fo.product_id = p.product_id
    GROUP BY fo.customer_id
)
SELECT c.customer_id,
       ov.cumulative_order_value,
       ov.order_frequency,
       ov.avg_price_point
FROM order_values ov
JOIN Customers c ON ov.customer_id = c.customer_id;

votes.sql:
SELECT 
    s.supplier_name,
    SUM(ps.total_value_purchased * er.avg_rate) AS total_purchase_eur
FROM Product_Suppliers AS ps
JOIN Suppliers AS s
      ON s.supplier_id = ps.supplier_id
JOIN (
        SELECT 
            strftime('%Y-%m', rate_date) AS month,
            AVG(eur_usd_rate) AS avg_rate
        FROM Exchange_Rates
        GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m', rate_date)
     ) AS er
      ON er.month = strftime('%Y-%m', ps.date_supplied_from)
GROUP BY s.supplier_id;
SELECT supplier_id, SUM(total_value_purchased) AS total_purchase_value_eur FROM Product_Suppliers GROUP BY supplier_id

WITH monthly_rate AS (
    SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', rate_date) AS year_month,
           AVG(eur_usd_rate) AS avg_rate
    FROM ExchangeRates
    GROUP BY year_month
)
SELECT SUM(ps.total_value_purchased / mr.avg_rate) AS total_purchase_value_euros
FROM Product_Suppliers ps
JOIN monthly_rate mr
  ON mr.year_month = strftime('%Y-%m', ps.date_supplied_from)
GROUP BY ps.supplier_id;
